Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the deep-dive into your payments flow. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can scope the auth/key mgmt work: 

Recap
- Primary use: FintechCo will call Redwood's hosted API from your backend to do document summarization and account-level embedding searches for risk and compliance.
- Traffic: estimated 3M tokens/month initially, spiking at EOD batch runs.
- Compliance: SOC2 + customer-controlled key rotation are hard requirements.

Open questions we promised to follow up on
1) Recommended auth pattern: API keys vs service accounts (JWT/OAuth) for multi-tenant environments.
2) Rotation and revocation: automated rotation cadence and HSM/KMS integrations.
3) Routing: how to pin requests to Dedicated vs Hosted based on route/policy.
4) Embeddings & rerank: where to run similarity search (FintechCo infra vs Redwood dedicated) and how keys are scoped.

Next steps (proposal)
- I'll loop in our Solutions Engineer (Rishi) and our Security Engineer (Neha) to answer the above in detail and propose a minimal integration checklist.
- Attachments: I've included a 1-page integration checklist and a spreadsheet template for key-management requirements (see attachments).
- Can we schedule a 30-min call next week to align on the auth approach and clarify rotation/ops? Suggested times: Tue/Wed 10-12 PT.

Thanks — I'll follow up internally and share a short readout.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — that looks good. A few follow-ups from our side before the call: 

1) For our infra reasons we prefer not to embed long-lived API keys in services. Ideally we'd use service accounts with JWTs that we can mint from our identity provider. Is Redwood able to accept JWT bearer tokens (OIDC) with per-tenant claims?

2) Rotation: we need automatic key rotation and immediate revocation on employee offboarding. We use AWS KMS and HashiCorp Vault today — can Redwood integrate with either for key wrapping or should we push keys into Redwood's KMS?

3) Embeddings: latency matters for in-app searches. Would you recommend running the similarity search inside our infra (using Redwood embeddings output) or having Redwood run the vector store with per-tenant isolation? Costs and egress are considerations.

4) For routing: how hard is it to make a route that sends high-priority requests to Dedicated nodes (in our VPC) while sending bulk/async batch traffic to Hosted? We like the idea of automatic fallback if Dedicated is at capacity.

We're available Wed 6/9 10:30-11:00 PT for a short sync. Priya will also bring our infra lead if needed.

Best,
Alex
Director of Engineering | FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com

Hey team — quick tech notes / proposed content for the send to FintechCo: 

JWT/OIDC support:
- Redwood supports OIDC bearer tokens validated against a JWKS endpoint. Required claims we recommend: iss, sub, aud (must match your Redwood client id), exp, iat, and an optional tenant claim (tid or tenant_id) for multi-tenant routing.
- Example: FintechCo mints short-lived JWTs (1-5m) from your IdP and presents them in the Authorization: Bearer <jwt> header. We validate signature + claims and map tenant_id -> account routing.

Key rotation / KMS integration:
- Options: (A) Customer-managed keys: FintechCo keeps wrapping keys in AWS KMS/Vault; Redwood stores encrypted provider-wrapped material and unwraps via an HSM-protected KMS integration. Pros: FintechCo full control over key lifecycle. Cons: slightly higher latency on first decrypt call.
- (B) Redwood-managed keys with customer rotation policy: Redwood hosts key material in our KMS/HSM and supports rotation API (rotate, revoke). Pros: simpler for ops; Cons: FintechCo gives up direct control.
- Immediate revocation: we support revocation hooks (API + push webhook) that can remove active API tokens and invalidate cached sessions.

Routing & fallback:
- We can create route tags per API key/tenant to pin to Dedicated (VPC) clusters. Policy engine supports rule: "route.priority == high -> Dedicated; else -> Hosted" and automatic fallback to a compatible Hosted model if Dedicated capacity is unavailable.

Embeddings / vector store recommendation:
- For lowest latency and customer control, run vector search in FintechCo's infra using Redwood embeddings: Redwood returns embedding vectors; FintechCo hosts vector DB (e.g., Milvus/Pinecone) and performs NN search.
- If FintechCo prefers managed ops, Redwood can provide an isolated per-tenant vector store (dedicated namespace), with egress controls and SLA.

I can draft a 1-page technical note with sample JWT header + curl examples. Neha — anything to add on compliance side?

—Dev
